title: Philadelphia Trivia Night

questions.q: Philadelphia's name comes from Greek words meaning what?
Which famous cracked bell is on display across the street from Independence Hall?
Which founding document was adopted at Independence Hall on July 4, 1776?
The statue on top of Philadelphia City Hall shows which man, the founder of Pennsylvania?
In the film Rocky, Rocky Balboa runs up the front steps of which building?
questions.a: The Philadelphia Museum of Art (renamed the Philadelphia Art Museum in 2025)

questions.q: Which sandwich of thin-sliced beef on a long roll, often with Cheez Whiz or provolone, is the city's best-known food?
On which day of the year does the Mummers Parade take place?
The Eagles won their first Super Bowl in February 2018 by beating which team?
Which river separates Philadelphia from Camden, New Jersey?
Boathouse Row, whose outline lights up at night, stands on the bank of which river?

notes: From Greek philos (loving) and adelphos (brother); see Philadelphia (Wikipedia), Etymology, or the city's own 'City of Brotherly Love' usage.
Liberty Bell displayed at the Liberty Bell Center, across Chestnut Street from Independence Hall; see Liberty Bell (Wikipedia) or nps.gov/inde.
Declaration adopted 4 July 1776 at the Pennsylvania State House (Independence Hall); see Independence Hall (Wikipedia) or nps.gov/inde.
Alexander Milne Calder's bronze William Penn statue tops the City Hall tower; see Philadelphia City Hall (Wikipedia).
Rocky steps; the museum rebranded as the Philadelphia Art Museum in Oct 2025, accept either.
Philly cheesesteak, credited to Pat and Harry Olivieri in the 1930s; see Cheesesteak (Wikipedia).
Mummers Parade held every New Year's Day since 1901; see Mummers Parade (Wikipedia).
Super Bowl LII, 4 February 2018, Eagles 41, Patriots 33, their first Super Bowl title; see Super Bowl LII (Wikipedia) or NFL.com.
The Delaware River divides Philadelphia and Camden, NJ, spanned by the Ben Franklin Bridge; see Delaware River (Wikipedia).
Boathouse Row sits on the east bank of the Schuylkill River, outlined in lights; see Boathouse Row (Wikipedia).
